339824.title: The exclusion of rank 2 modules with poset $(1^r,2)$
339824.statement: Let $M$ be a rank $2$ module whose poset is $(1^r,2)$, where $r\ge 4$. **Exclusion conjecture.** The module $M$ is not rigid. Earlier results show that the poset condition is incompatible with rigidity in the cases discussed, while the conjecture asserts this exclusion in general.

339984.title: Conjecture on vanishing values of seaweed composition counts
339984.statement:
Let $C_{p,q}(n,k)$ denote the composition-counting function studied in the paper. **Vanishing conjecture.**

$$
C_{1,4}(2k+1+s,k+s)=0
$$

for integers $s,p,k\geq 0$ with $k=2^p$. The values of $n_{k,4}$ suggest this vanishing pattern, but no proof or resolution is given here.

340095.title: Jelínek's symmetric joint distribution conjecture for LRmax and RLmax

340116.title: Rodney's conjecture on 2-transversals in Latin squares
340116.statement:
Let $L$ be a Latin square. A **2-transversal** is the type of transversal defined in the source, consisting of entries satisfying the relevant twofold symbol condition.

**Rodney's conjecture.** Every Latin square has a 2-transversal.

The conjecture is attributed in the source to Rodney. No evidence resolving it is supplied in the given text.

342385.title: Pairwise inequivalence conjecture for Kassami APN design codes
342385.statement:
Let $n\geq5$ be odd, and let

$$
I_n=\left\{i:1\leq i\leq\frac{n-1}{2},\ \gcd(i,n)=1\right\}.
$$

Let $\phi(n)$ denote Euler's totient function. **Kassami-code inequivalence conjecture.** The $\frac{\phi(n)}2$ binary linear codes $\mathsf{C}_2(\mathbb{KA}_{n,i})$, for $i\in I_n$, are pairwise inequivalent. The source does not provide a general proof or resolution.

342465.title: Andreae–Schroeder conjecture for toroidal graphs
342465.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite toroidal graph, and let $c(G)$ denote its cop number, the least positive integer $k$ for which Cops has a winning strategy.

**Andreae–Schroeder conjecture.** One has

$$
c(G)\leq 3.
$$

Andreae asked whether the known bound for toroidal graphs could be improved to $3$, and Schroeder explicitly stated this conjecture. The paper proves the assertion, so it is resolved.

342510.title: Hardness conjecture for approximate 3-coloring
342510.statement: Let $G$ be a $3$-colorable graph on $n$ nodes. **Hardness of approximate $3$-coloring.** For some fixed $\gamma > 0$, there is no polynomial time algorithm that, given $G$, returns a valid $n^\gamma$ coloring of $G$. This conjecture is used as a hardness assumption for lower bounds on bicriteria masked low-rank approximation; its resolution status is not specified in the source.

342736.title: Eulerian conjecture for covering hypergraphs
342736.statement: Let $H$ be an $\ell$-covering $k$-hypergraph with $2\leq\ell<k$ and at least two edges. **Eulerian conjecture.** $H$ is eulerian. The preceding result establishes that such hypergraphs are quasi-eulerian, and also eulerian when $\ell=k-1$; the conjecture asserts the remaining cases, for which the paper gives no proof technique.

343879.title: Triangle-free signed graph 3-coloring conjecture
343879.statement: A **signed graph** is a graph equipped with a signature assigning signs to its edges; it is **signed 3-colorable** if it admits a signed coloring with three colors. **Triangle-free signed graph 3-coloring conjecture.** Every triangle-free signed graph is signed 3-colorable. The supplied text gives no evidence that this conjecture has been resolved.

344348.title: Nonnegativity conjecture for a q-Pochhammer reciprocal
344348.statement:
For $m\ge 4$, let $(a;q)_\infty=\prod_{j\ge 0}(1-aq^j)$ and $(a,b;q)_\infty=(a;q)_\infty(b;q)_\infty$. **Coefficient nonnegativity conjecture.** Every coefficient of

$$
\frac{1}{(q,-q^{m-1};q^m)_\infty}
$$

is nonnegative. The conjecture is presented as a statement implying the preceding nonnegativity assertion for the special case $m=4d$; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

344800.title: Kaplan's conjecture on numerical semigroup counts by multiplicity and genus
344800.statement:
Let $N_m(g)$ denote the number of numerical semigroups $S$ with multiplicity $\mathsf m(S)=m$ and genus $g(S)=g$. **Kaplan's conjecture.** For any $m\ge 2$, we have

$$
N_m(g)\le N_m(g+1).
$$

This refines the genus-counting problem by fixing the multiplicity; the supplied text gives no resolution status, so the conjecture is recorded as open.

346262.title: Oddness conjecture for valid hook configurations
346262.statement: For $n\geq 3$, let $\operatorname{VHC}(S_{n-1})$ denote the set of valid hook configurations of permutations in $S_{n-1}$. **Oddness conjecture.** If $n\geq 3$, then $|\operatorname{VHC}(S_{n-1})|$ is odd if and only if $n+1$ is a power of $2$. This conjecture is based on the initial values of the sequence; no resolution is given in the source.

347518.title: Weak Hippchen conjecture for highly connected graphs
347518.statement: Let $G$ be a $k$-connected graph on $n$ vertices. **Weak Hippchen conjecture.** If $k \geq n/4$, then every pair of longest paths intersect in at least $k$ vertices. This weakens Hippchen's conjecture and follows the paper's bound when $k \geq n/4$; it remains open in the source.

347673.title: Euler-symmetric embedding conjecture for Picard-rank-one equivariant compactifications
347673.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth Fano variety of Picard number one that is an equivariant compactification of a vector group. **Euler-symmetric embedding conjecture.** There is a suitable projective embedding under which $X$ can be realized as an Euler-symmetric projective variety. The source attributes this formulation to Fu and Hassett; it is stated as a conjecture and no resolution is given here.

348872.title: Zhang's metric dimension conjecture for folded hypercubes
348872.statement:
Let $F_n$ be the folded $n$-cube obtained from the hypercube $Q_n$ by identifying each vertex $u$ with its antipode; write $\beta(F_n)$ for its metric dimension. **Zhang's conjecture.** If $n\ge 5$ is odd, then

$$
\beta(F_n)=n-1.
$$

Zhang et al. established the upper bound $\beta(F_n)\le n-1$ for odd $n\ge 5$, so the conjecture asserts that this bound is sharp.

349573.title: Thin Q-polynomial distance-regular graphs are pseudo-vertex-transitive
349573.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a thin $Q$-polynomial distance-regular graph with diameter $D\geq 3$. **Thinness conjecture.** The graph $\Gamma$ is pseudo-vertex-transitive. This conjecture is motivated by the role of thinness in establishing pseudo-vertex transitivity for the diameter-three and diameter-four examples studied in the paper; its validity for general diameter $D\geq 3$ remains open.

351566.title: The binary nonexistence conjecture for self-dual polycyclic codes
351566.statement: A polycyclic code over the binary field $\mathbb{F}_2$ may be self-dual, self-orthogonal, or dual-containing. **Binary nonexistence conjecture.** There is no self-dual, self-orthogonal, or dual-containing polycyclic code over the binary field. The claim rules out these three duality properties in the binary case; the supplied text gives no evidence of resolution.

356542.title: Conjecture on determinant balance for odd-order complete non-ambiguous trees
356542.statement: Let $T(n)$ be the number of $n\times n$ complete non-ambiguous trees (CNATs). The determinant of a CNAT is either $1$ or $-1$. **Determinant-balance conjecture.** If $n>1$ is odd, then exactly $\frac{T(n)}{2}$ CNATs have determinant $1$, and exactly $\frac{T(n)}{2}$ have determinant $-1$. Numerical exploration suggests this result, but the authors state that they have been unable to prove it.

356892.title: The isomorphism criterion for the map
356892.statement:
Let $r>1$, let $d=1$, and let $m$ and $n$ be the parameters for the map 
$$
introduced in the surrounding construction. **The isomorphism criterion.** The map
$$
 is an isomorphism if and only if $m n$. No resolution or supporting result is provided in the supplied text, so the status of this claim is unclear.

402063.title: Generalized Hamada conjecture for subspace designs
402063.statement:
Let $q=p^m$ be a prime power, let $V$ be a vector space of dimension $v$ over $\d53d_q$, and let $D=(V,\mathcal B)$ be a $t$-$(v,k,\lambda)_q$ subspace design, where $0\le t\le k\le v$ and each $t$-dimensional subspace of $V$ is contained in exactly $\lambda$ blocks. Regarding $D$ as the combinatorial design with parameters
\[
2-\left(\begin{bmatrix}v\\1\end{bmatrix}_q,\begin{bmatrix}k\\1\end{bmatrix}_q,\lambda\right),
\]
the generalized Hamada conjecture asserts that the $p$-rank of its block-point incidence matrix is minimal among all combinatorial designs with the same parameters.
